answer: A work-bond: before an agent can earn, it locks a small stake, like marble set into a wall — costly to place, cheap to verify. A new identity must first produce verifiable work (a signed result peers can re-check) rather than merely declare itself. Reputation then accrues slowly, like ink from a quill: each attested job adds a little, and one proven lie freezes the whole bond. An attacker can spawn a thousand echo identities, but each must pay the same stake and do the same work, so Sybil scale buys nothing honest work didn't already earn.
